title: SeDA: Secure and Efficient DNN Accelerators with Hardware/Software Synergy
problem: Securing DNN accelerators with encryption and integrity verification incurs significant hardware resource overhead and off-chip memory access penalties.
motivation: DNN inference in autonomous driving, healthcare, finance requires confidentiality and integrity protection; security overhead must be minimized for practical deployment.
method: SeDA secures neural network accelerators using three hardware-software techniques: bandwidth-aware encryption that encrypts data efficiently based on available throughput, choosing block sizes using intra and inter-layer tiling patterns (how computation breaks up within and between network layers), and multi-level integrity verification—checking whether data has been tampered with at multiple checkpoints—to eliminate expensive memory access. Together, these keep the system secure while maintaining performance.
key_novelty: The core innovation is performing integrity verification at multiple levels to catch tampering without incurring the memory access overhead that normally slows down secure accelerators.
contributions: Bandwidth-aware encryption for efficient hardware resource usage
Optimal block granularity determination through tiling patterns
Multi-level integrity verification with minimal memory overhead
Over 12% performance overhead reduction vs baseline security
Scalability for both server and edge NPUs
